scope: Theorem 4.6 (Cutoff entry with one compulsory component) of the manuscript “The critical logarithmic correction for the planar XY model” (preprints/The-critical-logarithmic-correction-for-the-planar-XY-model-October-5-2026/paper.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 216 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 5c357d1c416119fa), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF pages 32-33. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. The quote crosses a page break and includes whatever the extraction places there, such as a page number. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. AMVO has checked nothing about this claim.
statement: Fix the finite list of map norms and reserves just described. There are constants C, c > 0 such that the following holds for every sufficiently large fixed dyadic R, with P = R5 and the fixed period q. For every sufficiently large dyadic s satisfying (59), the assertions below hold uniformly in the finite volume. The threshold on s may depend on all preceding choices. A compatible torus or aligned free square has side at least sP; for a marked square its side is larger than the fixed multiple of sP needed to contain the compulsory region and its collars. In the square applications its ratio to sP tends to infinity. (i) There are plane activities K0 m which are real on real fields, negation-even, invariant under common translation by ω, and covariant under block translations and square symmetries. There are centered torus and free-square activities K0 G,m with ∥K0 m∥m,Aw,V , ∥K0 G,m∥m,Aw,V ≤ Ce−cR in each of the fixed norms. On every such finite graph a positive field-independent scalar cG,m makes (39) hold. If Dm(X) unwraps in a torus, its activity is exactly the plane activity. The same is true in a free square when Dm(X) misses the wall. (ii) In a free square with the center unit there are real periodic activities Kτ G,m and JG,m for which (40) holds with that same scalar. For a constant CR < ∞ independent of s, n, ∥Kτ G,m∥m,Aw,V ≤ Ce−cR , ∥JG,m∥m,Aw,V ≤ CRsCR . (60) The sector norm may use the slightly weaker weight and stronger regulator already reserved above. There is a fixed set C⋆,m of at most CR entry blocks, containing the full inflation of a square of side a fixed large multiple of P in observation-cell units around the source, such that JG,m(X) = 0 unless C⋆,m ⊂ X. (61) 32 Every block of C⋆,m is occupied in X in the subset functional. The full support of each summand of J(X) also occupies every padded dependency and the complete connecting, winding, or wall-reaching tag of every item in that summand. (iii) If the rectangle spanned by Dm(X) misses the source, then Kτ G,m(X, ψ) = K0 G,m(X, ψ + λX), (62) where λX is its local lift. This assertion uses the finite-square centered prescription if the support is near a wall. There are also centered-unit plane prescriptions Kτ ∞,m and J∞,m. Whenever Dm(X) misses the square wall under the centered aligned identification just specified, its prescription is exactly the plane one with background translated by (vn − v∞)/α. (63) This identity holds for both the unlabelled and labelled activities. The sufficient regions in all three copy statements include the padded supports and all occupied tags. The plane centered-unit prescriptions obey the same bounds as in (60), with their local plane norms.
